correctness.rationale: With centered covariance C=I−11ᵀ/n, the conditional two-contact loss for ordered edges e,f is tr(CP_eP_fP_e)=tr(P_eP_f)−1=n−3+(v_eᵀv_f)². The squared inner products are 1, 1/4 and 0 for identical, incident and disjoint edges. Equivalently the loss is tr((I−L_p/2)²)−1=n−3+tr(L_p²)/4. The unsigned incidence Gram matrix gives B_G≽I/2; the simplex KKT signs and normalization are correct. On the path the tridiagonal recurrence with zero exterior coordinates yields the displayed product of factors 1−r^i and 1−r^(m+1−i), all strictly positive; summing shows S_m/m→2/3 and hence both boundary and bulk limits. Subtraction gives q_1−q_2 proportional by a positive factor to r^(m−1)−r>0 for m≥3. For the separate gap benchmark the centered ramp gives an upper Rayleigh bound; the parabolic law attains it because its weighted Laplacian is triangular on polynomial-degree flags, with eigenvalues c k(k+1). Equality forces the centered ramp eigenvector and recursively determines the weights. At m=1 the only law gives loss zero, and m=2 is reflection-symmetric. At m=3 direct substitution gives losses 23/16 and 13/9, difference 1/144, with center-edge masses 1/4 and 2/5 for the two objectives.
residual_risks: Requires independent draws from the same fixed law and covariance I, not arbitrary worst-case initial disagreement or an adaptive schedule. The recorded 297 checked cases/groups include numerical comparisons of radicals and asymptotics; not all are exact rational assertions. The general result is analytic.
